arxiv-1701-05570.title: Solving an integral equation arising from the Ruin probability of long-term Bonus–Malus systems
arxiv-1701-05570.description: Abstract This article studies in detail the solution of an integral equation due to Rongming. The methods involve complex analysis. As an application, we find the ruin probability of a given Bonus–Malus system in a steady state. We obtain closed form solutions for the ruin probability in certain cases, and we characterize these cases.

Facilities: SOFIA (FIFI-LS), Spitzer (IRAC, MIPS), Herschel (PACS, SPIRE), ALMA, GALEX, Chandra, SDSS, 2MASS astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ) , sospex ( Fadda & Chamb
arxiv-2101-10966.creator: Dario Fadda, Seppo Laine, Philip N. Appleton
arxiv-2101-10966.description: Abstract We present new SOFIA [C II] and ALMA CO J=1→0 observations of the nearby asymmetric barred spiral galaxy NGC 7479. The data, which cover the whole bar of the galaxy and the counter-arms visible in the radio continuum, are analyzed in conjunction with a wealth of existing visible, infrared, radio, and X-ray data.

arxiv-2202-05920.title: Boosting Barely Robust Learners: A New Perspective on Adversarial Robustness
arxiv-2202-05920.creator: \name Avrim Blum \email avrim@ttic.edu
arxiv-2202-05920.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by \name Avrim Blum \email avrim@ttic.edu. We present an oracle-efficient algorithm for boosting the adversarial robustness of barely robust learners. Barely robust learning algorithms learn predictors that are adversarially robust only on a small fraction β ≪ 1 \beta\ll 1 of the data distribution. Our proposed notion of barely robust learning requires robustness with respect to a “larger” perturbation set; which we show is necessary for strongly robust learning, and that weaker relaxations are not sufficient for strongly robust learning.

arxiv-2210-11641.title: Model exploration in gravitational-wave astronomy with the maximum population likelihood
arxiv-2210-11641.creator: Ethan Payne, Eric Thrane
arxiv-2210-11641.description: Abstract Hierarchical Bayesian inference is an essential tool for studying the population properties of compact binaries with gravitational waves. The basic premise is to infer the unknown prior distribution of binary black hole and/or neutron star parameters such component masses, spin vectors, and redshift.

arxiv-2403-01754.title: Derivative-Free Optimization for Low-Rank Adaptation in Large Language Models
arxiv-2403-01754.creator: Feihu Jin, Yifan Liu, Ying Tan
arxiv-2403-01754.description: Abstract Parameter-efficient tuning methods such as LoRA could achieve comparable performance to model tuning by tuning a small portion of the parameters. However, substantial computational resources are still required, as this process involves calculating gradients and performing back-propagation throughout the model.

arxiv-2406-13734.title: A Unified Core Structure in Multiplex Networks: From Finding the Densest Subgraph to Modeling User Engagement
arxiv-2406-13734.creator: Farnoosh Hashemi, Ali Behrouz
arxiv-2406-13734.description: Abstract . In many complex systems, the interactions between objects span multiple aspects. Multiplex networks are accurate paradigms to model such systems, where each edge is associated with a type. A key graph mining primitive is extracting dense subgraphs, and this has led to interesting notions such as k k -cores, known as building blocks of complex networks.

pmc-11728648.title: Genomic Evolution and Phylodynamics of the Species Orthomarburgvirus marburgense (Marburg and Ravn Viruses) to Understand Viral Adaptation and Marburg Virus Disease’s Transmission Dynamics
pmc-11728648.creator: Claude Mambo Muvunyi, Nouh Saad Mohamed, Emmanuel Edwar Siddig, Ayman Ahmed
pmc-11728648.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In this review, we investigated the genetic diversity and evolutionary dynamics of the Orthomarburgvirus marburgense species that includes both Marburg virus (MARV) and Ravn virus (RAVV). Using sequence data from natural reservoir hosts and human cases reported during outbreaks, we conducted comprehensive analyses to explore the genetic variability, constructing haplotype networks at both the genome and gene levels to elucidate the viral dynamics and evolutionary pathways.

pmc-12510303.title: Comparison between the crystal structures of racemic and enantiopure aryl benzyl sulfoxides
pmc-12510303.creator: Maria Annunziata M. Capozzi, Angel Alvarez-Larena, Joan F. Piniella Febrer, Cosimo Cardellicchio
pmc-12510303.description: In literature reports about the comparison between the crystal structures of racemic and enantiopure compounds, minor differences have been observed between the conformations of an enantiopure compound and the conformations of the same enantiomer when they are a part of a racemic compound.

pmc-12633792.title: Drosophila Dpp and BMP signaling directly regulates dpp transcription for optimal ligand production
pmc-12633792.creator: Yan Zhang, Ying Feng, Xiaolei Ye, Yi Lin, Ling Zeng, Yuting Luo, Lin Zhou, Chenghao Shen, Weiqi Hu, Dong Yan, Xinhua Lin
pmc-12633792.description: Precise control of morphogen dosage in the source is essential for establishing developmental patterning and maintaining signaling stability. Here, we demonstrate that in Drosophila wing imaginal discs Decapentaplegic and BMP (Dpp/BMP) signaling modulates expression of the ligand Dpp through direct transcriptional auto-regulation. The results show that reduction of Dpp/BMP signaling upregulates dpp transcription, whereas enhanced signaling represses it.

pmc-12690009.title: Essential Anatomy for the Abdominal Wall Surgeon: Expert Consensus of Anatomical Concepts and Operative Steps for Posterior Component Separation
pmc-12690009.creator: Lawrence Nip, Samuel G Parker, Andrea Scala, Steve Halligan, Timothy A Rockall, Rhys Thomas, Pasquale Giordano, Gregory Simpson, Praminthra Chitsabesan, Marja Boermeester, Sarah Zhao, Alastair C J Windsor, Miguel Angel Garcia‐Urena
pmc-12690009.description: IntroductionAbdominal wall surgery is emerging as a new subspecialty with reconstructive operations becoming increasingly complex. Central to any surgical subspecialty is comprehensive anatomical knowledge, which can be enhanced by cadaver dissection. An expert panel convened to develop a consensus framework highlighting key anatomical concepts and operative steps for teaching posterior component separation.

pmc-13102554.title: Clinical efficacy of drug-eluting stents in the treatment of vertebral artery stenosis and analysis of factors contributing to stent restenosis
pmc-13102554.creator: Xiuping Wei, Zhi Ma, Huimin Wu, Haibo Jiang, Wenya Lan, Lili Xu, Mingyang Du, Hui Cao, Xin Wang, Feng Qiu
pmc-13102554.description: BackgroundVertebral artery stenosis, especially at the ostium, is a significant cause of posterior circulation ischemic events. Although drug-eluting stents (DESs) have demonstrated superior efficacy in reducing restenosis compared to bare-metal stents (BMSs), the specific incidence and predictors of in-stent restenosis (ISR) following DES implantation in patients with ostial vertebral artery stenosis (OVAS) remain inadequately investigated.

pmc-13258365.title: Suppressing Gate-Induced Drain Leakage with an Asymmetric Gate Design in HiPco CNT FETs
pmc-13258365.creator: Hui Ma, Senbiao Gu, Minglong Zhai, Honggang Liu
pmc-13258365.description: Carbon nanotube field-effect transistors (CNT FETs) hold great promise for extending Moore’s Law, yet their performance is critically limited by excessive off-state leakage, caused by band-to-band tunneling (BTBT) in narrow bandgap CNT channels. In this work, we overcome this long-standing bottleneck by introducing a co-design strategy that integrates a small-diameter HiPco CNT channel with a novel asymmetric gate architecture.

pmc-13455441.title: Herpes simplex virus encephalitis following acute brain injury: illustrative cases
pmc-13455441.creator: Allison K. Shay, Nicholas M. Cordero, Nam Dinh Phuong Nguyen, Jueria Rahman, Jack Zhang, Zachary L. Hickman, Gregory Kapinos, Laura Salgado-Lopez
pmc-13455441.description: BACKGROUNDHerpes simplex virus (HSV) is the most common cause of sporadic viral encephalitis in adults, yet HSV encephalitis (HSVE) occurrence in the setting of traumatic brain injury (TBI) and intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) is rarely documented. Brain injury induces systemic immunosuppression that may predispose to viral reactivation.
